PHASE.NAME: Persistent Configurable LSP Runtime
PHASE.GOAL: Resolve FIX/C2 and FIX/L3 by replacing per-request LSP spawning with a reusable manager and configurable language-server commands.

DATA_FLOWS.FLOW: MCP LSP requests resolve a language and root, obtain a pooled LSP connection, send didOpen as needed, then dispatch hover/definition/references.
Config-provided LSP server commands override built-in defaults without changing existing fallback behavior.
Post-v2.6.0 development advances Cargo/install metadata to v2.6.1 so release freshness guards remain meaningful after new commits.

STEPS.step-1: Added LspConfig and optional lsp.servers command overrides with default fallback behavior.
STEPS.step-2: Introduced an LSP connection manager with lifecycle, request ids, didOpen tracking, shutdown cleanup, and graceful missing-binary errors.
STEPS.step-3: Threaded runtime Config into LSP tool handling while keeping MCP stdio behavior stable.
STEPS.step-4: Advanced Cargo.lock/Cargo.toml package version to 2.6.1 for post-release freshness.
STEPS.step-5: Advanced install.sh default version to v2.6.1.
STEPS.step-6: Updated release smoke verification tag expectations to v2.6.1.

RISKS.RISK: Returning references from pooled process state requires avoiding borrowed values across locks; use owned Arc-managed connections.
External LSP binaries may be absent in CI; tests should use protocol helpers or fake server processes rather than requiring rust-analyzer.
